clue.text: Look away from gory corpse

indicators.note: taking one word away from another tells us to remove those letters from it

parts.note: gory means bloody, covered in blood
lo is an old word for look, as in 'lo and behold'

explanation.surface: Someone is told to avert their eyes from a gruesome dead body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look away from gory' reads as advice to the squeamish, but it says take LO (look) away from BLOODY (gory).
explanation.definitionFit: A body is the usual word for a dead person's remains, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Attempt to keep exercise nearly all on two feet

indicators.note: one piece keeping another holds it inside

parts.note: a bid is an attempt
PE is physical education, school exercise

indicators.note: nearly means all but the final letter

parts.note: all is taken as the word itself before trimming

explanation.surface: A try at keeping fit by walking almost everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to keep' signals a container, and 'nearly' trims the last letter; 'on two feet' looks like part of the surface but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bipedal describes walking on two legs, so it means going about on two feet.

clue.text: Each Apostle could take his own line from such a figure

definitions.text: Each Apostle could take his own line from such a figure

parts.words: Each Apostle could take his own line from such a figure
parts.note: there were twelve Apostles, so a shape with twelve sides gives one side each

explanation.surface: Each of the twelve disciples follows a separate path from a central figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'line' sounds like a calling or a creed, but it is a side of a geometric figure, and there were twelve Apostles.
explanation.definitionFit: A twelve-sided polygon has exactly as many sides as there were Apostles.

clue.text: One present that's taken and not returned?

definitions.text: One present that's taken and not returned?

parts.words: One present that's taken and not returned
parts.note: reads like a gift accepted and never given back, but describes a person present at gatherings who takes free hospitality and never reciprocates

explanation.surface: A gift is accepted and never handed back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' seems a noun meaning gift; it is an adjective, someone in attendance. 'Taken' is what they help themselves to, and 'not returned' is the favour never repaid.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponger who takes what others provide without giving anything back fits this description of a guest who never repays.

clue.text: Make good traveller's song

parts.note: a rep is a travelling salesman
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: A travelling salesman's song makes amends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'traveller's' with its 's' means 'traveller has', joining REP to AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: To make good something broken is to mend it, a synonym phrase.

clue.text: Newly realised net value coming after some time

indicators.note: letters realised newly are made again in a fresh form

explanation.surface: A financial update gives the asset's net value as recently realised.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventual describes what happens in the end, after a period of time has passed.

clue.text: Aim, perhaps, for something quite unusual

definitions.meaning: the word aim shows I (Roman one) placed in A and M (Roman thousand), so it exemplifies the phrase
a rare thing, found only once among very many

explanation.surface: An ambition, perhaps, for achieving something remarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: In Roman numerals I is one and M a thousand: put I in A + M and you get AIM, hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes someone or something rare, exceptional among a great many.

clue.text: Queen featured in silly sketch

indicators.note: a piece featured in another appears inside it

parts.note: daft means silly
R is short for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: The Queen appears in a comic sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sketch' seems a comedy skit; it is a rough version, a draft.
explanation.definitionFit: A draft is a preliminary sketch or outline of a piece of work.

clue.text: Followers join up in flanks of Easter rising

indicators.note: one piece in another sits inside it
in a down clue, rising means the letters read upwards, backwards
the flanks of a word are its first and last letters
up in a down clue means the word is turned backwards

parts.note: to join is to unite

explanation.surface: Supporters link arms at the edges of the Easter Rising.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'rising' and 'up' read upwards in a down clue: 'rising' turns R...E from the flanks, 'up' turns the join word to ETINU, and 'in' sets one inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue is a body of attendants who follow an important person.

clue.text: NSW too sunny? Aim to get out here

indicators.note: getting letters out of their order sets them free to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A tourist in New South Wales finds it too sunny and plans an escape somewhere cooler.
explanation.walkthrough: NSW is New South Wales, the Australian state where this snowy range lies, so 'here' points to the place the surface describes.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition 'here' stands for a cold Australian range in New South Wales, a place to escape the sun.

clue.text: Literary philistine on reflection criticises start of Dickens work

indicators.note: a reflection shows things the other way round, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a musical or literary work

explanation.surface: A reviewer, reconsidering, attacks the opening of a Dickens novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' turns the whole run round. Mr Podsnap, in Dickens's Our Mutual Friend, is the smug complacent philistine who gave English the word 'Podsnappery'.
explanation.definitionFit: This Dickens character embodies smug, narrow-minded middle-class complacency, so he is a philistine from literature.

clue.text: Stylish Jumbo, good for power and height

indicators.note: 'good for power and height' means good stands in place of those two

parts.note: Jumbo was a famous circus elephant, and the name is used for any elephant

explanation.surface: An elephant is praised for being graceful, strong and tall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' signals a swap: in ELEPHANT, the PH (power and height) is replaced by G (good).
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant and stylish are synonyms, both describing graceful, tasteful appearance.

clue.text: One taking a turn on stage

definitions.text: One taking a turn on stage

parts.words: One taking a turn on stage
parts.note: a stage turn sounds like a variety act, but refers to the pantomime hero who heard the bells telling him to turn again and go back to London

explanation.surface: A performer does their act in a variety show.
explanation.walkthrough: In the story, Bow Bells call 'Turn again, Whittington, Lord Mayor of London', and he turns back; he is a stock hero of British Christmas pantomime.
explanation.definitionFit: The pantomime title character literally turns back on hearing the bells, and is played on stage every Christmas.

clue.text: Shelter needed round sweet pea

indicators.note: one piece placed round another means it encloses it

parts.note: lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
gum is a chewy sweet

explanation.surface: A sweet pea plant needs protection around it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweet pea' looks like the flower, but 'sweet' is wordplay and the definition is just 'pea'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pea is a pod-bearing plant of the bean family, an example of the wider class.

clue.text: Sweet's gone bad by end of heatwave

parts.note: gone means past, over and done with
ill can mean bad, as in ill fortune

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A sweet has spoiled in the hot weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet's' reads as possessive but is 'sweet is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastille is a small chewy or medicated sweet, so the general word covers it.

clue.text: I'm getting round America in railway car

indicators.note: the pieces go in the railway word, inside it

parts.note: a railway line
taken as written, without its apostrophe
O is round in shape
US is the United States

explanation.surface: Someone travels round the United States by rail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'railway car' looks like one phrase; 'car' alone is the definition, and 'getting' just links IM to O.
explanation.definitionFit: A limousine is a large luxurious car, often chauffeur-driven.

clue.text: Turn up in a tie, showing self-confidence

indicators.note: one piece in another goes inside it

parts.note: a tether is a rope that ties an animal

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word reads backwards

parts.note: a turn in a game is a go

explanation.surface: Someone arrives wearing a tie and looks self-assured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn up' looks like 'arrive', but it is GO reversed (OG), placed in TETHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone together is composed and self-assured, an informal sense of the word.

clue.text: One who might put woman in box to persuade member of panel

definitions.text: One who might put woman in box

parts.note: to con someone is to talk them into something by trickery
a juror is one member of a jury panel

explanation.surface: Someone sawing a lady in half is trying to win over a juror.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the stage illusion of putting a woman in a box and sawing her in half.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage magician performs the classic trick of placing an assistant in a box, so the definition describes him by that act.

clue.text: Note as to how keeping clubs is a source of profit

parts.note: C is a musical note

indicators.note: one word keeping another holds it inside

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs, the card suit

explanation.surface: A memo explains how holding onto clubs earns money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' puts C (clubs) inside HOW; 'to' links the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A cash cow is a business or product that reliably generates profit, an idiom.

clue.text: Missile launcher, the first of eight

definitions.meaning: in a rowing eight, the oarsman nearest the bow is seat number one

explanation.surface: A rocket launcher is the first of eight weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: Rowing crews number seats from the bow, so the bow rower is the first of an eight.
explanation.definitionFit: An archer shoots arrows from a bow, and in rowing the bow seat is number one in the boat.

clue.text: Possible home for African river spirit is erected

indicators.note: erected in a down clue means set upright, read from bottom to top

parts.note: the Aire is a river in Yorkshire
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: An African river spirit's home is built.
explanation.walkthrough: 'African river' looks like the Niger; it is the AIRE, an English river, and with GIN the pair is turned upwards by 'is erected'.
explanation.definitionFit: An African could well come from this West African country, so the definition is a cryptic example.

clue.text: No seat is given up a 'ound a club, perhaps

indicators.note: a Cockney dropping of round, so these letters go round the next piece
in a down clue, given up means turned upwards, read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a pew is a church seat

explanation.surface: A Cockney complains there's no seat on a hound, while a club is mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: ''ound' is 'round' with the R dropped, Cockney style: A goes round-inside WEPON, which 'is given up' makes by turning both words upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A club is one example of a weapon, a blunt instrument for hitting.

clue.text: Russian GP better for treatment in this city

indicators.note: letters given treatment are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A Russian doctor is the better choice for medical care in this city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'GP' (a family doctor) looks like a medical term but is just two letters of fodder rearranged with RUSSIAN and BETTER.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue points to a city on the Baltic that is Russia's second city, formerly the capital.

clue.text: Desirable fish got with a line

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A desirable fish caught on a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal describes the most desirable or perfect option.

clue.text: Love of that woman is entering cold hearts

indicators.note: one piece entering another goes inside it

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
H is the abbreviation for hearts, the card suit
her refers to a woman already mentioned

explanation.surface: A woman's love melts frosty hearts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' signals a container; 'of' is a link, and 'cold hearts' gives the two outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To cherish someone is to love and care for them dearly, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Basket girl found by head of jetty

indicators.note: the girl is found just by the head, the first letter, of the jetty word, so she sits right after it

parts.note: a pier is a jetty projecting into the sea
Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl and her basket are spotted at the end of a pier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found by head of' puts the girl immediately after the first letter of the jetty word, splitting it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pannier is a basket, especially one carried by a donkey or slung on a bicycle.

clue.text: Rich provider we will free from gaol

parts.note: to spring a prisoner is to help them escape from gaol

explanation.surface: A wealthy benefactor promises to break us out of prison.
explanation.walkthrough: A wellspring is a source of water, and figuratively an abundant source of anything.
explanation.definitionFit: A wellspring is a plentiful source, so it is a rich supplier of whatever flows from it.

clue.text: High land in Thames area

indicators.note: a word found in a phrase lies within its letters

explanation.surface: There is high ground in the Thames valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A mesa is a flat-topped hill with steep sides, an elevated tableland.
